chunks: My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, who said: A man asked Abu al-Hasan (AS) while he was circumambulating (the Ka'bah), saying to him: Tell me about the Generous. He replied to him: Verily, your word has two meanings: If you are asking about the created, then the generous person is one who gives what Allah, the Mighty and High, has made obligatory on him, and the miser is one who withholds what Allah has made obligatory on him. And if you mean the Creator, then He is the Generous whether He grants or He withholds, because if He grants to a servant, He grants him what is not his, and if He withholds, He withholds what is not his.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Generous created and the Generous Creator according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to clarify the semantic duality of 'Al-Jawad' within the context of Divine Names, distinguishing between the relative generosity of creatures and the absolute generosity of Allah. For the created, generosity is defined by the fulfillment of obligatory duties (fara'id), while for the Creator, His giving is bestowing what is not His (since all belongs to Him) and His withholding is retaining what is not His, demonstrating that His attributes are not bound by human limitations. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on Allah's absolute ownership and the derived nature of human attributes.
